situation: Any chemical in the eye
immediate: Flush at once with clean running water (eyewash station if there is one) for at least 15 minutes, or longer if the SDS says so. Hold the eyelids open and roll the eye. Remove contact lenses if they come out easily.
doNot: Do not delay flushing to find the SDS. Do not rub the eye. Do not use drops, neutralizers or another chemical.
ppe: Eye protection, splash goggles for the helper if splashing continues
escalate: Any corrosive or caustic product (oven cleaner, drain cleaner, concentrated detergent), pain that continues, blurred vision, redness or swelling after flushing
manager: Call 911 or go to emergency care and bring the SDS. Record the incident and the product. Start a corrective action.

situation: Splash of diluted sanitizer or sanitizer solution
immediate: Flush with clean water for 15 minutes. Check the SDS for the product strength.
doNot: Do not wait to see if it settles. Do not rub.
ppe: Goggles when mixing or changing sanitizer
escalate: Pain or redness that continues after flushing, any vision change
manager: Offer medical care. Record the incident. Check that the dispenser, bucket or test strips are being used correctly.

situation: Chemical on skin
immediate: Remove contaminated clothing, gloves and jewelry. Rinse the skin with running water for at least 15 minutes, or as the SDS says. Wash gently with mild soap once rinsed.
doNot: Do not apply neutralizers, creams or ointments unless the SDS says to. Do not scrub hard.
escalate: Chemical burn, blistering, large area, pain that continues, product is corrosive or caustic
manager: Seek medical care. Bag contaminated clothing and keep it. Record the incident. Check glove and apron use.

situation: Caustic or concentrated product on skin (oven cleaner, degreaser concentrate, dish machine detergent)
immediate: Start rinsing immediately with large amounts of running water and keep going for at least 20 to 30 minutes unless the SDS says otherwise. Remove contaminated clothing while rinsing.
doNot: Do not stop early because the pain eases, since damage can continue. Do not use vinegar or other neutralizers.
ppe: Chemical gloves, apron, face shield when pouring or changing concentrate
escalate: Always seek medical care for caustic burns
manager: Call 911 or take the person to emergency care with the SDS. Record the incident. Review how the product is handled and what PPE is worn.

situation: Chemical soaks through clothing or shoes
immediate: Remove the clothing and footwear immediately. Rinse the skin underneath for at least 15 minutes.
doNot: Do not leave wet clothing in contact with skin. Do not take contaminated clothing home to wash.
escalate: Skin burns, large area, pain
manager: Medical care if needed. Bag the clothing for disposal or separate laundering. Record the incident.

situation: Fumes or strong vapors, person feels dizzy, has a headache or burning throat
immediate: Move the person to fresh air if it is safe to do so. Keep them seated and calm. Ventilate the area from a safe distance.
doNot: Do not go into a vapor area without protection. Do not let the person go back until the area is cleared.
ppe: None for the helper unless trained and equipped; stay out of the vapor
escalate: Trouble breathing, wheezing, chest pain, confusion, fainting, symptoms that continue
manager: Call 911 if breathing is affected. Otherwise call Poison Control. Record the incident and find the source.

situation: Chlorine or bleach smell after mixing products or heavy use
immediate: Leave the area, open doors and run exhaust fans. Keep others out. Treat any coughing or eye irritation as exposure.
doNot: Do not try to clean it up or add another product. Do not re-enter until the smell has gone.
ppe: None until the area is clear
escalate: Coughing that continues, shortness of breath, any person feeling unwell
manager: Call 911 for breathing problems. Record the incident. Check which products were mixed or stored together.

situation: Dish room steam or chemical mist causes irritation
immediate: Move out of the dish room to fresh air. Check the dish machine for a chemical leak or a feed problem.
doNot: Do not keep working in the area. Do not override machine alarms.
ppe: Gloves and goggles for the person checking
escalate: Breathing difficulty, symptoms that continue
manager: Stop the machine if it is leaking. Call the chemical vendor or service company. Record the incident.

situation: Chemical swallowed (any amount)
immediate: Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 immediately and follow what they say. Have the product name and the SDS ready. Rinse the mouth with water if the person is awake and able to spit.
doNot: Do not make the person vomit. Do not give food, milk or drink unless Poison Control says to.
escalate: Always call Poison Control. Call 911 for drowsiness, trouble breathing, seizures, burns around the mouth or severe pain
manager: Call 911 if instructed. Keep the container. Record the incident. Review storage and labeling.

situation: Chemical stored in a food or drink container is drunk by mistake
immediate: Treat it as a swallowed chemical. Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222. Keep the container and its contents.
doNot: Do not pour out the container. Do not make the person vomit.
escalate: Always call Poison Control or 911
manager: Find out how it happened. Remove all chemicals from food containers at once. Record the incident and start a corrective action.

situation: Small spill, a few ounces, product known and contained
immediate: Keep people away and put up a wet-floor sign. Put on the PPE listed on the SDS. Wipe or absorb the spill and bag the waste. Rinse the area and let it dry.
doNot: Do not wash the spill into a floor drain unless the SDS allows it. Do not mix products.
ppe: Gloves, goggles, apron as the SDS says
escalate: Spill spreads, fumes, anyone feels unwell, product is unknown
manager: Record if anyone was exposed. Replace used spill supplies. Check why it spilled.

situation: Large spill, spreading, or in a walkway
immediate: Evacuate the area and keep others away. Close the doors to the area if it is safe. Call the manager. Use the SDS to decide on PPE and response.
doNot: Do not clean it up if you are not trained and equipped. Do not allow people to walk through it.
ppe: Only as the SDS says, trained staff only
escalate: Fumes, a spill you cannot control, an unknown product, a fire or reaction risk
manager: Call 911 or the chemical vendor's emergency line. Keep the area closed until it is cleared. Record the incident and start a corrective action.

situation: Spill of unknown or unlabeled product
immediate: Treat it as hazardous. Isolate the area and keep people out. Try to identify the product from nearby containers without touching it.
doNot: Do not smell it. Do not touch it. Do not mix it with water or other products.
ppe: Gloves and goggles at minimum if you must approach
escalate: Any fumes, smoke, heat, or reaction
manager: Call the vendor or emergency services if it cannot be identified. Record the incident. Find out where it came from.

situation: Spill on or near electrical equipment
immediate: Turn off the power at the breaker if it is safe to reach. Keep people away.
doNot: Do not spray water or wipe around live equipment. Do not touch wet cords.
escalate: Sparks, smoke, burning smell, or any shock
manager: Call 911 for fire or shock. Call the electrician or service company. Do not use the equipment until it is checked.

situation: Container leaking or damaged in storage
immediate: Wear PPE and move the container into a tray or spill bucket if it is safe to do so. Keep it upright. Stop the leak.
doNot: Do not move a container that is leaking heavily. Do not stack other items on it.
escalate: Fumes, a leak you cannot stop, product reacts with other items
manager: Call the vendor for disposal advice. Record the incident. Check storage and ordering.

situation: Broken glass and chemical together
immediate: Keep people away. Wear heavy gloves and goggles. Pick up glass with tongs or a scoop and place it in a puncture-proof container. Absorb the liquid.
doNot: Do not use bare hands or a mop on glass. Do not wash it into a drain.
escalate: Anyone cut or exposed, fumes
manager: Get medical care for cuts that have chemicals in them. Record the incident.

situation: Bleach mixed with ammonia, acid or another cleaner
immediate: Leave the area at once and keep others out. Open doors and turn on exhaust fans from a safe place. Call the manager.
doNot: Do not go back in to clean up. Do not try to neutralize the mixture.
escalate: Coughing, burning eyes or throat, difficulty breathing, anyone unwell
manager: Call 911 for breathing problems. Keep the area closed until it is aired and cleared. Record the incident and retrain staff.

situation: Wrong dilution or wrong product in a spray bottle or sanitizer bucket
immediate: Stop using it. Label it clearly and set it aside. Rinse any surface it touched that is food contact.
doNot: Do not top up or add other products. Do not pour into another container.
escalate: Anyone exposed, skin or eye irritation
manager: Discard it as the SDS says. Re-mix with the correct product and test strips. Record it if food contact was possible.

situation: Chemical put in the wrong dispenser or dish machine feed
immediate: Stop the machine. Do not run any more loads. Isolate the product.
doNot: Do not rinse dishes and use them. Do not keep running the machine.
escalate: Any fumes, foaming, or heat
manager: Call the chemical vendor. Rewash and sanitize everything that went through. Record the incident.

situation: Dish machine chemical leak or concentrate spill
immediate: Turn the machine feed off and keep people away. Contain the spill with absorbent. Use PPE listed on the SDS.
doNot: Do not mop it into the drain. Do not mix with sanitizer.
escalate: Fumes, skin or eye exposure, a spill you cannot control
manager: Call the chemical or machine service. Record the incident. Check the feed lines and containers.

situation: Refrigerant leak in a walk-in or cooler (hissing, oily residue, strong smell)
immediate: Move people out of the area and keep the doors open for air. Switch off the unit if it is safe to reach the switch.
doNot: Do not stay in a closed walk-in. Do not use open flames or smoke near it.
escalate: Anyone dizzy or short of breath, a strong smell, a leak you cannot reach
manager: Call 911 if anyone is affected. Call the refrigeration service. Move and check the food. Record the incident.

situation: Gas smell or suspected carbon monoxide
immediate: Leave the building and take everyone out. Leave doors as they are. Call from outside.
doNot: Do not turn lights or equipment on or off. Do not use a phone or lighter inside. Do not re-enter.
escalate: Always call 911 and the gas company
manager: Do not re-enter until emergency services say so. Record the incident and have equipment checked before use.

situation: Aerosol or pressurized can near heat or damaged
immediate: Move it away from heat if it is safe. Keep people away.
doNot: Do not puncture, heat or crush it. Do not throw it in a hot trash area.
escalate: Venting, hissing, heat, fire
manager: Call 911 if it vents or catches fire. Record the incident. Review storage.

situation: Chemical splashed on or near food
immediate: Stop work and isolate the food. Do not use any food that may have been splashed. Keep it separated and labeled.
doNot: Do not rinse food and serve it. Do not sell or use it.
escalate: Any food that was served or sold
manager: Discard the food. Record what was thrown out. Review the cause. Notify the manager.

situation: Chemical on a food-contact surface, utensil or equipment
immediate: Stop using it. Wash, rinse and sanitize the item as the SDS and your cleaning standard say. Check it before use.
doNot: Do not just wipe it dry. Do not use it until it has been cleaned and checked.
escalate: A surface that cannot be cleaned, or food that touched it
manager: Discard any food that touched it. Record the incident. Review how chemicals are used near food.

situation: Chemicals found stored with or above food
immediate: Move them at once to the chemical storage area, below and away from food. Check nearby food for contamination.
doNot: Do not leave them. Do not use any food that was touched or splashed.
escalate: Leak, spill or damaged container
manager: Throw out any food that may be contaminated. Record the finding and correct the storage.

situation: Unlabeled or unknown chemical container found
immediate: Do not use it. Keep it separate from food and other chemicals. Do not open it.
doNot: Do not smell it. Do not pour it into another container. Do not guess what it is.
escalate: Leaking, fumes, or a reaction
manager: Ask the vendor or staff what it is. Dispose of it as hazardous waste if it cannot be identified. Record it.

situation: Pest control or vendor chemical applied in the kitchen
immediate: Keep staff and food out of the area until the vendor says it is safe. Ask for the product name and SDS.
doNot: Do not clean up the vendor's product. Do not re-enter early.
escalate: Any staff feeling unwell
manager: Cover or remove food and food-contact surfaces as the vendor says. Keep the application record and SDS.

situation: Employee feels unwell after cleaning
immediate: Move them to fresh air and rest. Find which product they used.
doNot: Do not make them go back to the task. Do not guess what the cause is.
escalate: Breathing difficulty, severe symptoms, fainting
manager: Call Poison Control for advice or 911 if serious. Record the incident. Review ventilation and PPE.
